Verdict: REVISEThe restriction proof and the two exact transfer identities are correct under the note’s stated original-profile and canonical-mark hypotheses. I found no overlooked support-restoration conflict, event overlap, or sign error in
$$R(F)=R(L)+R(\mathrm{Right})-S_s$$
and
$$\mu(F)=\mu(L)+\mu(\mathrm{Right})-N_s-S_s+d_s.$$
The package nevertheless needs one substantive proof dependency resolved and one deletion criterion stated more precisely:The unmarked-positive-branch reduction in §5 uses  $R(\text{branch})\ge0$ . That bound is neither proved nor explicitly supplied as an established result in the provided material. Minimality does not supply it.For a negative separator,  $R(\text{branch})\ge S_s$  is the condition for deletion without increasing the margin, and a uniform sufficient guarantee of preserving negativity. It is not necessary for preserving negativity in a particular family whose negative margin is already known.These are revisions to the claimed consequences, not a refutation of the separator identities. I have not assumed any earlier verdict, verified the reported executions, or treated the finite controls as a general proof.1. Required revisions to the counterexample reductionsWrite  $J$  for a branch containing  $s$ , and  $K$  for its complementary restriction, also containing  $s$ .1.1 The unmarked positive branch needs an additional reserve boundSuppose  $s$  is positive,  $J$  contains no other positive source, and neither canonical side of  $s$  is marked in  $J$ . With the allocation margin
$$\mu(I)=N(I)-G(I)+R(I),$$
we have
$$N(J)=1,\qquad G(J)=0,\qquad \mu(J)=1+R(J).$$
Because  $J$  has no separator mark,  $d_s=0$ . The proved transfer identity therefore gives
$$\mu(F)=\mu(J)+\mu(K)-1
      =R(J)+\mu(K),$$
or equivalently
$$\boxed{\mu(K)=\mu(F)-R(J).}$$
Thus the proposed removal follows if  $R(J)\ge0$ . The issue is the unproved step in §5:
$$1+R(J)\ge1.$$
The displayed ledger
$$R(J)=S(J)+2|F_{\mathrm{mix}}(J)|-|E(J)|$$
does not make that inequality automatic. It requires the quantitative bound
$$|E(J)|\le S(J)+2|F_{\mathrm{mix}}(J)|.$$
Neither separator legality nor the event and tile partitions prove this bound.Minimality also does not close the gap. A proper legal restriction of an owner-minimal counterexample has nonnegative margin, which gives only
$$1+R(J)\ge0.$$
In particular, in the integral count model, this still permits  $R(J)=-1$ .There is a precise unresolved boundary here. If  $F$  is owner-minimal with negative integral margin, then both  $\mu(J)$  and  $\mu(K)$  are nonnegative. Consequently,
$$R(J)\ge-1,\qquad R(J)\le\mu(F)\le-1.$$
The remaining algebraically possible case is exactly
$$\boxed{
R(J)=\mu(F)=-1,\qquad
\mu(J)=\mu(K)=0.
}$$
This is not a constructed physical U/rotor counterexample. It identifies the case that the written argument has not excluded.The economical repair is one of the following:Cite and invoke an independently established reserve bound that applies to these actual complete restrictions.Prove the narrower bound  $R(J)\ge0$  for branches with exactly the unmarked positive separator.State this deletion reduction conditionally on  $R(J)\ge0$ .If the referenced signed-reserve note already establishes the needed bound, the repair is to identify that result and check its hypotheses. The supplied package does not presently let me verify that dependency.1.2 The negative-branch “only when” statement overstates necessitySuppose  $s$  is negative and  $J$  has no positive sources. Then
$$N(J)=G(J)=0,\qquad \mu(J)=R(J),$$
so the transfer identity gives
$$\boxed{\mu(K)=\mu(F)+S_s-R(J).}$$
The different deletion criteria are therefore:Desired conclusionExact condition $\mu(K)\le\mu(F)$  $R(J)\ge S_s$  $\mu(K)<0$ , for a particular known  $\mu(F)<0$  $R(J)>S_s+\mu(F)$ Hence the sentence that a branch can be safely removed “only when  $R(J)\ge S_s$ ” is too strong if “safely” means merely that the complementary restriction remains a counterexample.A precise replacement is:A branch without positive sources can be removed without increasing the margin whenever  $R(J)\ge S_s$ . This guarantees a smaller counterexample using only the fact that the full margin is negative. For a specified full margin, the exact criterion is  $R(J)>S_s+\mu(F)$ .The preceding claim in §5 is correct:
$$\mu(F)\ge0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mu(L)+\mu(\mathrm{Right})\ge S_s$$
at a negative separator. Two individually nonnegative branch margins do not establish the full inequality.2. Mandatory support restoration: the legality proof passesHere is an independent proof of the central restriction claim, including the support/support case.For a retained owner set  $I$ , put
$$P_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}P_i,\qquad
O_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}(P_i\cup T_i).$$
The selected set is
$$\left(\bigcup_{i\in I}T_i\right)\setminus P_I.$$
Thus supports whose endpoint consumers are deleted are restored automatically.Take  $L=A\cup\{s\}$ . Suppose  $x$  is selected in  $L$ , with retained producer  $i$ , and suppose that  $y\in O_L$  is adjacent to  $x$  with
$$y\ne a_i(x).$$
We derive a contradiction.First consumption. Both  $a_i(x)$  and  $y$  are occupied in the full fusion. If  $x$  were still selected there, it would have two distinct occupied neighbors. Full feasibility therefore forces
$$x\in P_j$$
for an endpoint owner  $j$ . Since  $x$  is selected in  $L$ , this owner was removed, so  $j\in B$ .The edge
$$a_i(x)x$$
joins endpoints of owners  $i$  and  $j$ . If  $i\in A$ , it violates the no-cross-edge hypothesis. Hence  $i=s$ .Locate the conflicting neighbor. Intrinsic feasibility of  $s$  excludes  $y\in O_s$ , because  $x\in T_s$  and  $y\ne a_s(x)$ . Choose an owner  $k\in A$  with  $y\in O_k$ .If  $y\in P_k$ , then  $yx$  is already a forbidden  $A$ – $B$  endpoint edge.The remaining case is  $y\in T_k$ . Let
$$b=a_k(y)\in P_k.$$
We have  $b\ne x$ : otherwise  $x$  would be an endpoint of both  $k\in A$  and  $j\in B$ , contrary to endpoint ownership uniqueness.Second consumption. In the full fusion,  $y$  has distinct occupied neighbors  $b$  and  $x$ . Full feasibility therefore forces  $y$  to be an endpoint of an owner  $\ell$ .If  $\ell\in A$ , the edge  $yx$  is forbidden.If  $\ell\in B$ , the edge  $by$  is forbidden.Therefore  $\ell=s$ .But now  $y\in P_s$  is a second original occupied neighbor of  $x\in T_s$ , contradicting intrinsic feasibility of  $s$ .This closes the restored support/support case. No restored support has been omitted.Two details matter:Intrinsic feasibility must mean uniqueness among all original occupied neighbors, including original supports. That is exactly what the supplied hintrinsic says.The proof repeatedly uses fixed original anchors and fixed original occupied sets. Recomputing or shrinking an original source’s support data after restriction would change the problem.Completeness beyond the abstract feasibility predicateThe written degree and matching adapter is also valid under the retained original-source assumptions:For each retained  $i$ ,  $O_i\subseteq O_L$ , so every original occupied neighbor used to establish an endpoint’s degree remains present.Retaining whole sources retains their unchanged matching edges.Disjoint endpoint ownership prevents collisions between those retained matching edges.These facts establish the additional physical conditions described in §2. They are not encoded in the conclusion of separator_side_is_feasible, whose formal conclusion concerns selected-support neighbor uniqueness.3. Directed events: the disjoint partition passesWith the supplied event definition, an event is a source-labelled triple
$$(i,x,y)$$
such that
$$i\in I,\quad x\in P_i,\quad y\in P_I,\quad
y\notin O_i,\quad x\sim y,$$
with  $x,y$  in the same fixed tile.Because  $O_i$  is original and fixed, restriction cannot create an event. Thus
$$E(L),E(\mathrm{Right})\subseteq E(F).$$
For any event of  $F$ , let  $j$  be the unique endpoint owner of its target  $y$ . If neither  $i$  nor  $j$  is  $s$ , their endpoint adjacency prevents them from lying on opposite exclusive sides. If either is  $s$ , the restriction containing the other owner contains both. This proves coverage.For disjointness, an event lying in both restrictions would have:its labelled tail owner in both owner sets, hence equal to  $s$ ;its target owner in both owner sets, by endpoint ownership uniqueness, hence also equal to  $s$ .Then  $y\in P_s\subseteq O_s$ , contradicting the event condition  $y\notin O_s$ .Therefore
$$\boxed{
E(F)=E(L)\mathbin{\dot\cup}E(\mathrm{Right}).
}$$
Repeated contacts and recurring owners cause no problem: the counted objects are the actual labelled events, not edges of a simplified source contact graph.4. Mixed full tiles: the proof passes, with the stated diagonal boundaryFix a full endpoint tile  $Q$  of  $F$ , and examine the separator’s original profile
$$C=P_s\cap Q.$$
Under the connected-or-empty profile hypothesis, the possibilities are exhaustive:Original separator profileComplement in the fixed squareEmptyFour-cycleOne vertexThree-vertex pathTwo adjacent verticesEdgeThree verticesSingletonFour verticesEmptyEvery nonempty complement is connected. Since  $Q$  is full, each complement vertex is an endpoint owned exclusively by  $A$  or  $B$ . If both sides occurred, a path between them in the complement would contain an  $A$ – $B$  endpoint edge. Thus all complement endpoints belong to one side, and  $Q$  is full in the corresponding restriction.The “mixed” qualifications also survive:If  $Q$  is full in both restrictions, every vertex belongs to their common endpoint set  $P_s$ . It is originally full in  $s$ , so it is excluded from both mixed-full sets.A tile mixed in a restriction remains mixed in  $F$ . A removed source cannot originally fill that same tile, because all four of its endpoints would overlap retained endpoints.A mixed full tile of  $F$  that is full in a restriction cannot become originally full there: that original owner would also make it originally full in  $F$ .Therefore
$$\boxed{
F_{\mathrm{mix}}(F)
=
F_{\mathrm{mix}}(L)\mathbin{\dot\cup}
F_{\mathrm{mix}}(\mathrm{Right}).
}$$
The diagonal exception is genuine and correctly excludedLabel the four corners cyclically  $v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3$ . If one allowed
$$P_s\cap Q=\{v_0,v_2\},$$
one could put  $v_1$  on the  $A$  side and  $v_3$  on the  $B$  side. Those two vertices are not adjacent. The full tile would then appear only after combining the restrictions.That defeats the tile-cover argument if diagonal separator profiles are admitted. It is not a counterexample to the written theorem, which explicitly excludes them.The relevant distinction is between an original separator profile and a profile produced by mixing owners. A mixed diagonal elsewhere does not invalidate this proof. The dangerous configuration is a diagonal in the original profile of the shared separator.The supplied material states the connected-profile property as a hypothesis. The two Lean files do not establish that every permitted U/rotor phase and dimension satisfies it. Consequently, the combinatorial theorem passes under that hypothesis; the universal catalogue application still depends on the asserted physical catalogue fact. Finite phase controls cannot replace that fact.Reserve identityOriginal negative mass satisfies ordinary inclusion-exclusion:
$$S(F)=S(L)+S(\mathrm{Right})-S_s.$$
Combining it with the two disjoint partitions yields
$$\boxed{R(F)=R(L)+R(\mathrm{Right})-S_s.}$$
A singleton has no foreign event and no mixed full tile, so  $R(\{s\})=S_s$ . The shared negative mass is subtracted exactly once in binary gluing. No general submodularity or supermodularity assertion is needed.5. Actual marks and the positive sign of  $d_s$ : the proof passesThe mark argument works provided a canonical side is a fixed side of the original positive source, and marking is the stated existence of an actual witness touching its positive endpoint protector.The exclusion of an unconsumed foreign-support witness deserves the following explicit justification. Let  $p\in P_i$  be the positive protector, and let a putative foreign support witness  $y\in T_k$ ,  $k\ne i$ , be adjacent to  $p$ . Its anchor  $a_k(y)\in P_k$  is distinct from  $p$ ; equality would contradict endpoint ownership uniqueness. If  $y$  were unconsumed, it would therefore have two distinct occupied neighbors,
$$p,\qquad a_k(y),$$
contradicting feasibility. Thus a foreign occupied witness must be an endpoint.For positive  $i\in A$ , an endpoint witness owned by  $B$  would give a forbidden cross edge. All its witnesses consequently remain in  $L$ , and its marks are unchanged. The argument for  $B$  is symmetric.For positive  $s$ , each fixed canonical side is marked in  $F$  exactly when it is marked in at least one restriction. This is Boolean union on sides, not a count of witness vertices.Writing  $M_s(L)$  and  $M_s(\mathrm{Right})$  for the two separator-side mark sets,
$$d_s=|M_s(L)\cap M_s(\mathrm{Right})|.$$
Hence
$$N(F)=N(L)+N(\mathrm{Right})-N_s$$
and
$$G(F)=G(L)+G(\mathrm{Right})-d_s.$$
Substitution into  $\mu=N-G+R$  gives
$$\boxed{
\mu(F)=\mu(L)+\mu(\mathrm{Right})-N_s-S_s+d_s.
}$$
The sign is positive because  $G$ , whose overlap is subtracted in its own inclusion-exclusion formula, enters  $\mu$  with a minus sign.For  $r$  branches, a side marked in  $m$  branches contributes  $m$  to the sum of branch mark counts and  $1_{\{m>0\}}$  globally. Their difference is
$$m-1_{\{m>0\}}=\max(0,m-1).$$
This proves the stated  $D_s$  correction and the multibranch formulas.The absence of positive duplicate-mark fixtures is not a proof failure here. The written witness-set argument covers  $d_s>0$ ; the controls do not establish its physical occurrence or provide its general proof.6. Which minimality reductions are established?Choose a negative-margin complete feasible fusion with the least number of original sources. Because  $A,B$  are nonempty, both separator restrictions are proper. The legality theorem therefore allows minimality to be applied to each:
$$\mu(L)\ge0,\qquad \mu(\mathrm{Right})\ge0.$$
Zero-charge separator. Here  $N_s=S_s=d_s=0$ , so the full margin is the sum of two nonnegative margins. A zero-charge articulation is excluded. This requires no reserve lower bound.Positive separator with a duplicated side. Here
$$\mu(F)=\mu(L)+\mu(\mathrm{Right})-1+d_s.$$
If  $d_s\ge1$ , the right side is nonnegative. This reduction is valid.Applying it to all partitions of the components after deleting  $s$  shows that each canonical separator side can have witnesses in at most one such component in a minimal counterexample. Multiple witnesses or owners within that same component are not excluded.Unmarked positive branch. This reduction requires the reserve bound identified in §1.1 above.Negative separator. The shared mass threshold is real. Nonnegative proper restriction margins alone do not give a contradiction. The exact deletion and nonincrease criteria are those in §1.2.There is also a minor connectivity qualification in §1 of the note. A connected source contact graph implies that the two restricted source contact graphs are connected. To conclude that their endpoint graphs are connected additionally requires each original  $P_i$  to be connected. Tilewise connected profiles alone do not imply global endpoint connectivity. If global connectivity is part of the established U/rotor catalogue, the sentence is valid; otherwise use “source contact graphs.” This distinction does not affect the transfer identities or the minimality argument over all complete feasible fusions.7. Written proof, Lean, and controls have different scopesOn inspection, the supplied Lean arguments faithfully express the following three propositions:DeclarationWhat the supplied proof establishesseparator_side_is_feasibleSelected-support neighbor uniqueness after restriction, under the displayed abstract anchor, ownership, intrinsic-feasibility, full-feasibility, and no-cross hypothesesdirected_event_lies_on_a_separator_sideCoverage of full-family directed events by the two restrictionsseparator_sides_have_disjoint_directed_eventsDisjointness of those directed event setsThe imported consumption lemma has the correct logical content. The restriction theorem does not need a separate keep separator assumption: when the exceptional case occurs, the proof identifies an already retained producer with the separator.The source does not formalize the physical U/rotor catalogue, endpoint degree and matching completeness, the square-profile complement lemma, mixed-full-tile counts, canonical marks, charges, reserve inequalities, or either complete margin formula. Those remain written mathematics. That limitation agrees with the note’s stated formalization scope.The displayed example has consistent arithmetic:
$$3+16-1=18,\qquad 3+15-1=17.$$
That checks the arithmetic only. Actual reconstruction of the eight-source example, its entire parameter family, the control totals, compilation, and axiom audit are not certified by this review.The central structural reduction can be retained. Resolve or condition the unmarked-positive-branch reserve bound, correct the negative-branch necessity wording, and keep the physical catalogue assumptions distinct from the three abstract Lean results. The unrestricted mixed U/rotor allocation inequality and rectangular-grid equality remain open.
